constraint_decided_it: O16 observed value is declared S4 -> E1, and S21 Measurement is NOT a subclass of S4 Single Observation (both are siblings under S27 Observation; S21's applicable-property list does not carry O16). Answer A asserts 'S21 Measurement (subclass of S4 Single Observation)' and hangs O16 off S21, which is out of domain. A's second violation: it attaches E54 Dimension to an I2 Belief, but I2 Belief is a subclass of E2 Temporal Entity, while P43 has dimension is E70 -> E54 (quantified dependent 0,n:1,1 on one E70 Thing) and O12 has dimension is S15 -> E54 -- no declared property connects a Belief to a Dimension. Answer B commits no domain/range violation and correctly reads the decisive boundary from the E16 Measurement scope note (the measurement is 'the initial transition from physical reality to information'; inferring properties from image material 'is not regarded as an instance of E16 Measurement, but as a subsequent instance of E13 Attribute Assignment'), and its 'E16 is a subclass of S21 in the harmonised model' is exactly the SIG's decision in t1458 ('Change S21 Measurement to superclass of E16 Measurement'), confirmed by the current declarations.
better_modelling: Sequencing: S2 Sample Taking producing an S13 Sample from the E20 Biological Object, then an S4 Single Observation (not S21, whose outcome slot is a dimension) with O24i/P39 measured or O8 observed pointing at the specimen/sample and O16 observed value -> an E73 Information Object / E90 Symbolic Object whose P190 has symbolic content carries the nucleotide string. The measured/observed thing takes P39 measured (E16 -> E18, quantified as necessary on E16) or O24 measured (S21 -> S15), NOT P16 used specific object, whose scope note is about tools, instruments and raw materials -- B borrowed P16 from the half of the E16 scope note that governs the empirical basis of a subsequent E13 Attribute Assignment. Phylogenetic placement: I5 Inference Making, J1 used as premise -> I4 Proposition Set, J2 concluded that -> I2 Belief (the clade placement), and the bootstrap support as J5 holds to be -> I6 Belief Value, which is declared as 'any encoding of the value of the truth of an I2 Belief ... expressed in terms of discrete logic, modal logic, probability, fuzziness, or any other adequate representational system'. External accession: E31 Document (its scope note states 'Documentation databases are regarded as instances of E31 Document') P70 documents the E20, P1 is identified by an E42 Identifier.
reasoning: A is wrong on two declared constraints: O16 observed value has domain S4 and S21 is a sibling of S4 under S27, not its subclass, so A's outcome slot does not exist on the class it chose; and E54 Dimension cannot attach to an I2 Belief because I2 is a subclass of E2 while P43 requires E70 and O12 requires S15. A's archive citation t1188 is honest and accurately qualified, and its 'the model does not adjudicate storage' is argued from absence rather than from a thread showing the question open, which the strict rubric disallows. B has no domain/range error, is right that E16's scope note makes tree-building a subsequent E13 Attribute Assignment rather than part of the measurement, and its E31 Document / P70 / P1 pointer is directly endorsed by E31's scope note; but it is suboptimal because it uses P16 used specific object where P39 measured (required on E16) or O24 measured is prescribed, misses S2 Sample Taking / S13 Sample while claiming CRMsci has no sample-extraction class, and over-claims that no class houses a support statistic when CRMinf I6 Belief Value is declared for exactly that. B's Minimality citation is loose (Minimality governs when the CRM declares a class, not what an instance store holds), but the 'Extensions of CIDOC CRM' passage it also cites says almost verbatim what it claims.
